title: CHAPTER SEVEN. On the attributes of God; essential properties not accidents
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): CHAPTER SEVEN. Concerning ye attributes belonging toward God. Thus far ye divine names have been: there follow ye attributes, which after ye manner belonging toward properties almost consequent upon ye nature belonging toward God as for our capacity somehow it was sketched stand, by which every perfection belonging toward God's essence more fully unto us is declared. That attributes first in divine matters found use, Daniel Heinsius, a man belonging toward wide learning, learnedly teaches (Aristarchus sacer, chapter 2, p. 42). Commonly essential or natural properties plus perfections belonging toward God they are called, which indeed are not qualities that upon God's essence happen, but God's very essence itself. For which reason a priori or in ye thing itself from ye essence or among themselves they are not distinguished, but formally plus by our mode belonging toward conceiving, nor more plus less do they admit.
pass_b_english: CHAPTER SEVEN. On the attributes of God.

Thus far have been the divine names: there follow the attributes, which are after the manner of properties almost consequent upon the nature of God as it was somehow sketched for our capacity, by which every perfection of God's essence is more fully declared to us.

That attributes first found use in divine matters, Daniel Heinsius, a man of wide learning, teaches learnedly (Aristarchus sacer, chapter 2, p. 42). They are commonly called essential or natural properties and perfections of God, which indeed are not qualities that happen upon God's essence, but God's very essence itself. For which reason they are not distinguished a priori or in the thing itself from the essence or among themselves, but formally and by our mode of conceiving, nor do they admit more and less.
source_text: CAPUT SEPTIMUM, De attributis DEI. Adeo huc usque sunt nomina divina: Sequuntur attributa, quae sunt instar proprietatum, naturam Dei, ut ea pro captu nostro aliquo modo adumbrata fuit, quasi consequentium, quibus omnis perfectio essentiae Dei nobis plenius declaratur. Attributa in divinis primum invenisse usum, erudite docet diffusae eruditionis vir, DAN. HEINSIUS, Aristarchi sacri cap. 2., pag. 42. Vulgo dicuntur proprietates essentiales, naturalesve & perfectiones Dei, quae sane non sunt qualitates, quae essentiae Dei accident, sed ipsissima Dei essentia. Qua de causa neque distinguuntur a priori aut reipsa ab essentia aut inter se, sed formaliter, nostroque concipiendi modo, neque recipiunt magis & minus.
